title: Symbolics.com, the first .com
hook: The first .com address was registered in 1985 by a maker of AI computers.
peek: On 15 March 1985, a Massachusetts computer company called Symbolics registered symbolics.com. It was the first .com domain name ever, and decades later the address is still online, now as a small museum of internet history.
lede: Every website ending in .com follows one that came first. On 15 March 1985, Symbolics, a computer maker in Cambridge, Massachusetts, registered symbolics.com. It was the first .com domain name. There was no rush to follow: only a handful of other .com names were registered that whole year, and anyone who wanted one could simply ask.

bullets.text: Symbolics built Lisp machines, powerful workstations designed to run Lisp, a programming language popular in artificial intelligence research. Its customers were mostly universities, research labs and big companies.
Only six .com names were registered in 1985. After symbolics.com came bbn.com, think.com, mcc.com, dec.com and northrop.com, all belonging to computer and engineering firms.
The company faded in the 1990s, but the name stayed registered. In 2009 symbolics.com was sold to an investment firm, which turned it into a page about the history of the internet.
Domain names only existed because Paul Mockapetris designed the Domain Name System in 1983. It replaced a single shared list of computer names with a system that could grow.
